A decision said in conversation and never written into a changelog, a standard or a workbook is in no file, so no sweep can find it. AND WHICH NUMBERED QUESTION EACH ONE ANSWERS (2026-09-30). Founder: “when I asked you to create one decision log and other files recording all decision no matter where I make that decision - how does not include updating with questions I am answering - they are not decision in your mind or what?” His answers to Q51, Q52 and Q53 WERE in the decision log from the moment he gave them — what I never did was carry them into the other file that holds the same decision, the master's own answer column, which is his PFS rule. Then I fixed it by inventing a SECOND home for answers, which is how two files come to disagree. So an answer names its question HERE, in the one log, and the master's answer column is printed from this file. One decision, one place, every destination fed from it.

TODAY, when money moved in or out in amounts large enough that WHEN it moved would decide the percentage, the Return states nothing and the screen shows the dollar walk alone. That person — someone actively adding money — is the one who most needs a rate and currently never sees one.
HIS RULING: show the exact rate there instead. Where the walk now says there is no percentage, it will read that counting when you added money, the rate was X% a year.
WHY THIS IS SAFE, measured: the two methods are not different answers. The window Return divides the gain once by a straight-line average of the money at work; the money-weighted rate compounds each amount over its own days and solves for the rate. On $100,000 with $10,000 added on 1 July and $118,000 at the end, they give 7.6161% and 7.6341% — 0.018 of a percentage point apart. They can never be far apart, because the window Return REFUSES the moment its straight-line shortcut could be off by more than a percentage point. So this fills the gap it leaves and never contradicts it: one return is visible at a time.
WHERE IT CAME FROM: the figure was built 2026-07-14 as its own card on the old Invest screen, and the Performance design he approved on 2026-09-25 (mock v14) removed that card. The function has been correct and reached by no screen since.

rows.subject: A CD bought through a broker is priced like a bond; a CD bought from a bank yields its rate

Before: every CD showed its interest rate as its yield to maturity — my rule of 2026-10-08, which assumed every CD was bought from a bank at face value.

rows.subject: In the time-weighted return, money that moves on a day counts for that whole day
rows.plain: The time-weighted return counts money that arrives on a day as there for that whole day, and money taken out as gone for that whole day: that day's growth is the evening value ÷ (the previous evening's value + money added − money taken out) − 1. A new account opened with $10,000 and worth $10,050 that evening returned +0.50% that day (+$50); worth $9,800, −2.00% (−$200). Vanguard worth $50,000, $10,000 added in the morning, $60,300 that evening: +0.50% (the $300 was earned on $60,000). Before: the money counted as arriving at the end of the day — the first deposit into a new account could not be measured at all, a value below the money just added was refused as a broken record, and the Vanguard day read +0.60%.
